theorem_statement:
General amplitude-mixture law (as claimed, with two qualifications recorded in gaps G1-G2). Let H be a stationary Gaussian field on X = R^d/(L Z^d), d >= 2, V = L^d, satisfying SG's contracts (SG Sections 4-7: COUNT (11)-(12), CONTACT/ENVELOPE (13)-(19) with the all-mark envelope H_SG(b,k) = C(1+|b|+k)^(2d) exp[-c(b^2+k^2)] at SG lines 388-394 valid for 0<r<=r_0, SELECT (21), FAR (22) at lines 473-480, ledger (23) and near representation at lines 486-502, coefficient c_q = C_H in (24)/(27) with 0 < c_q < infinity (line 509), the pointwise asymptotic (4) for the canonical Borel representative (lines 56-58, 508-512), finite expected critical count (line 293-296), and the field moment E||H||_C4^(2d) < infinity (SG (7) line 114 or (R4) lines 86-88, 117-118)). Let A be a (0,infinity)-valued random variable independent of H, with arbitrary law, and put F = A H and m := E[A^(-2/3)] in (0,infinity]. Then, for the F-side versions of all densities and conditional laws defined as the A-mixtures of the fixed-amplitude versions (Preliminaries P3 below):
(i) COUNT (F Morse with distinct critical values a.s.; ST's Borel elder selector (5) counts each finite H0 bar of F once; the pair formula ST (3)/SG (11) in unnormalized-mixture form and the two-height kernel ST (4)/SG (12), whose mixture version is finite at every fiber p != q, ell = b - b' > 0), CONTACT and SELECT hold for F for every such A.
(ii) ENVELOPE holds for F iff m < infinity. When m < infinity, H^F(b,k) := E[A^(-2) H_SG(b/A,k/A)] is an envelope with SG's r_0 and integral k^(-2/3) H^F db dk = m * integral k^(-2/3) H_SG db dk. When m = infinity no envelope exists (for any r_0' > 0 and any nonnegative Borel H'(u,b,k)).
(iii) If m < infinity then FAR holds for F, nu_F(ell) ~ m C_H ell^(-1/3) and E N^F_t / V ~ (3/2) m C_H t^(2/3) as ell, t -> 0, both directly from nu_F(t) = E[A^(-1) nu_H(t/A)], m_F(t) = E[m_H(t/A)] by dominated convergence, and consistently from ST's conditional structural theorem applied to F with C_F = m C_H.
(iv) If m = infinity then ell^(1/3) nu_F(ell) -> infinity and t^(-2/3) m_F(t) -> infinity (Fatou).
Consequently, among independent multiplicative amplitudes, the -1/3 law survives exactly for {A : E[A^(-2/3)] < infinity}, with coefficient E[A^(-2/3)] C_H; for AMP's power law this is alpha > 2/3 with E[A^(-2/3)] = a^(-2/3) alpha/(alpha-2/3), reproducing AMP (16). Process (Poisson) limits, non-independent amplitudes and non-multiplicative non-Gaussian fields are not covered.

proofs.part: P. Preliminaries: scaling identities, mixture versions, and bounds on nu_H (all re-derived)
proofs.proof:
Notation. X = R^d/(L Z^d), d >= 2, V = L^d (SG lines 20-22). H is SG-admitted: C4 version, E||H||_C4^(2d) < infinity (SG (7) line 114 under (A4), or (R4) lines 86-88; SG line 117-118: all field-norm moments used have order <= 2d). F = A H with A:(0,infinity)-valued, independent of H. m = E[A^(-2/3)].

P1 (pathwise scaling, fixed s > 0). sH has the same critical points as H, Hess(sH) = s Hess H (same inertia since s > 0), critical values scaled by s (distinctness preserved), and the same elder pairing because {sH >= h} = {H >= h/s} (AMP lines 131-140, (8)): ell^(sH)_i = s ell^H_i, b -> s b, k = ell/dist^3 -> s k, x and u unchanged. ST's selector: with D_f(p) = sup{lambda in Q : lambda < f(p), exists z in D with f(z) > f(p) chain-connected to p in {f > lambda}} (ST (5), lines 129-131), the set of admissible real lambda is a down-set (the chain condition is monotone in lambda), so its supremum over any dense subset is the same real number; since {sf > lambda} = {f > lambda/s} and lambda < sf(p) iff lambda/s < f(p), D_(sf)(p) = s D_f(p) and the Morse/distinct locus G is s-invariant; hence sigma(p,q,sf) = sigma(p,q,f) (ST lines 134-139). The type indicator tau in ST (2) is invariant and Delta_(p,q)(sH) = s^(2d) Delta_(p,q)(H), so W^(sH) = s^(2d) W^H and V^(sH)_r = s^(2d) V^H_r.

P2 (linear rows). U_r in ST (6)/SG (13) is linear: U_r(sH) = s U_r H. The target v_r(b,k) = (b - k r^3/2, -k r^2, 0, 12k, (0,0)_i) (ST (7)) is linear in (b,k): v_r(b,k) = s v_r(b/s, k/s). Likewise O_(p,q)(sH) = s O_(p,q)(H) and (b,0,b',0) = s (b/s,0,b'/s,0).

P3 (mixture versions). For nonnegative measurable Phi of the field, E[Phi(F)] = integral E[Phi(sH)] P_A(ds) (independence + Tonelli). Densities: U_r(sH) has density pi^(sH)_r(v) = s^(-(2d+2)) pi^H_r(v/s), so U_r F has density pi^F_r(v) = E[A^(-(2d+2)) pi^H_r(v/A)] in [0,infinity] (Tonelli; it integrates to 1, hence is finite a.e.). Conditional law: let Q^(sH)_r(.|v) be the s-dilation of SG's canonical Q^H_r(.|v/s) (SG (16), line 352, multiplied by s). For Borel sets B (field) and C (R^(2d+2)), P(F in B, U_r F in C) = integral P(sH in B, s U_r H in C) P_A(ds) = integral_C [ integral Q^(sH)_r(B|v) pi^(sH)_r(v) P_A(ds) ] dv. Thus kappa^F_r(B,v) := integral Q^(sH)_r(B|v) pi^(sH)_r(v) P_A(ds) is a disintegration of the joint law of (F, U_r F) along U_r F, and Q^F_r(.|v) := kappa^F_r(.,v)/pi^F_r(v) is a regular conditional law wherever 0 < pi^F_r(v) < infinity. Consequently, for every nonnegative measurable Psi of the field,
  (P3a)  pi^F_r(v) E_(Q^F_r)[Psi | v] = integral pi^(sH)_r(v) E_(Q^(sH)_r)[Psi | v] P_A(ds)   in [0,infinity].
Taking v = v_r(b,k) and Psi in {V_r sigma, V_r, V_r(1-sigma)} and using P1-P2 (E_(Q^(sH)_r)[V_r sigma | v_r(b,k)] = s^(2d) E_(Q^H_r)[V_r sigma | v_r(b/s,k/s)], pi^(sH)_r(v_r(b,k)) = s^(-(2d+2)) pi^H_r(v_r(b/s,k/s))):
  (T1)  B^F_r(b,k) = E[A^(-2) B^H_r(b/A, k/A)],  P^F_r(b,k) = E[A^(-2) P^H_r(b/A,k/A)],  Phi^F_r(b,k) = E[A^(-2) Phi^H_r(b/A,k/A)],
where B_r = 12 pi_r(v_r) E_(Q_r)[V_r sigma] (ST line 383, SG (23)), P_r := 12 pi_r(v_r) E_(Q_r)[V_r] (unselected product), Phi_r := 12 pi_r(v_r) E_(Q_r)[V_r (1-sigma)] (failure product). The same argument on the two-site observation O_(p,q) gives for the two-height kernel of ST (4)/SG (12)
  (T2)  K^F_sel(p,q,b,b') = E[A^(-2) K^H_sel(p,q,b/A,b'/A)],
and, integrating over b (substitution b = A b'' at fixed A, an exact linear change of variable on R with Jacobian A) and over p != q, then Tonelli over A,
  (T3)  nu_F(ell) = V^(-1) integral integral K^F_sel(p,q,b,b-ell) db dp dq = E[A^(-1) nu_H(ell/A)]   in [0,infinity],
which is AMP (9) (line 160) for an arbitrary positive independent A with the same proof. Since dist(p,q) is unchanged by amplitude, (T3) holds separately for the near part (dist < r_0) and the far part (dist >= r_0) with the same r_0. Counting: N^F_t = #{i : A ell^H_i <= t}; by independence and Borel measurability of the barcode in the field (SG lines 548-552), E[N^F_t | A] = V m_H(t/A), so
  (T4)  m_F(t) := E N^F_t / V = E[m_H(t/A)],
the general form of AMP (10) (line 187). Total mass: E B_F = E B_H < infinity (AMP line 150; SG lines 293-296 and AMP (5) lines 97-106 give E B_H <= E #Crit(H)/2 < infinity), so integral_0^infinity nu_F = E B_H / V < infinity.

P4 (bounds on the canonical nu_H). Let g(u) = u^(1/3) nu_H(u), g_near, g_far likewise, for the canonical representative of SG (12) split at r_0.
(a) Near part, all u > 0: SG lines 498-502 give, for the specific representative and every ell > 0, ell^(1/3) nu_(H,near)(ell) = integral 1{k >= ell/r_0^3} B_((ell/k)^(1/3))(b,k,u) /(3 k^(2/3)) db dk d sigma. The indicator restricts to r = (ell/k)^(1/3) <= r_0, where 0 <= B_r <= H_SG (SG (19), ST line 388). Hence g_near(u) <= K_near(u) := (|S^(d-1)|/3) integral_R integral_(k >= u/r_0^3) k^(-2/3) H_SG(b,k) dk db <= K_near := (|S^(d-1)|/3) I_SG < infinity, I_SG := integral_R integral_0^infinity k^(-2/3) H_SG db dk (finite by SG (19) line 394). Moreover K_near(u) -> 0 as u -> infinity (tail of a finite integral), and explicitly K_near(u) <= C exp(-c u^2/(2 r_0^6)) for u >= 1 from the Gaussian factor of H_SG.
(b) Far part. SG (22) (lines 473-480): 0 <= nu_(H,far)(ell) <= C for 0 < ell <= 1, so g_far(u) <= C u^(1/3) -> 0 as u -> 0. For a bound valid for ALL u (SG states only (22) on (0,1] and 'any fixed compact positive-lifetime band has a finite local bound', lines 481-482), re-derive SG's own estimate keeping ell: on {dist(p,q) >= r_0} the covariance Sigma_O of O_(p,q) satisfies lambda I <= Sigma_O <= Lambda I uniformly (SG lines 473-475: rank (9), continuity, compactness), so p_O(v) <= (2 pi)^(-(d+1)) lambda^(-(d+1)) exp(-|v|^2/(2 Lambda)); the Gaussian regression given O = v has mean linear in v with coefficients bounded uniformly over this compact separated domain and covariance at most the unconditional one, and W <= C(1+||H||_C2)^(2d), so E[W | O = v] <= C(1+|v|)^(2d) using E||H||_C2^(2d) < infinity. At v = (b,0,b-ell,0), |v|^2 = b^2+(b-ell)^2 = ell^2/2 + 2(b-ell/2)^2. Integrating over b in R and the pair domain (measure <= V^2): nu_(H,far)(ell) <= nu_(cand,far)(ell) <= C_far (1+ell)^(2d) exp(-ell^2/(4 Lambda)) <= G_far for every ell > 0. This is exactly SG's argument with the ell-dependence of the exponent tracked; it uses nothing beyond SG's displayed floor/upper bound and 2d-th moment (see gap G1).
(c) Hence G := sup_(u>0) g(u) <= K_near + G_far < infinity; g(u) -> C_H = c_q as u -> 0 (SG (4), a pointwise statement for the canonical representative, lines 56-58 and 508-512); and nu_H(u) <= C exp(-c u^2) for u >= 1 (both parts).
(d) h(u) := u^(-2/3) m_H(u) = u^(-2/3) integral_0^u nu_H <= u^(-2/3) integral_0^u G s^(-1/3) ds = (3/2) G, and h(u) -> (3/2) C_H (SG (4), count form). Alternatively, without (b): h <= C on (0,delta] from the asymptotic and h <= delta^(-2/3) E B_H/V on [delta,infinity) by finite total mass.

P5 (pointwise finiteness lemma, no moment on A). Fix N >= 0, C, c > 0, and (b,k) with k > 0. phi(a) := a^(-N) (1 + (|b|+k)/a)^(2d) exp(-c (b^2+k^2)/a^2) is a continuous function of a in (0,infinity) with phi(a) -> 0 as a -> 0 (the exponential beats every power since k > 0) and phi(a) <= a^(-N)(1+|b|+k)^(2d) bounded as a -> infinity; so M_N(b,k) := sup_a phi(a) < infinity and E[phi(A)] <= M_N(b,k) for EVERY law of A. The same holds with (b, b-ell), ell > 0, in place of (b,k), because b^2+(b-ell)^2 >= ell^2/2.

Nothing else: no bound or moment on A.

proofs.part: (i) COUNT, CONTACT and SELECT hold for F for every positive independent A
proofs.proof:
COUNT. (a) Morse/distinct a.s.: P(A > 0) = 1 and SG Section 4 (lines 236-296) gives H Morse with distinct critical values a.s.; by P1 the same holds for F = AH realization-wise (AMP line 143). (b) Selector: ST's sigma (ST lines 125-139) is everywhere Borel on fields; by P1 sigma(p,q,F) = sigma(p,q,H) on each realization, and ST's once-counting (lines 141-168) is a fact about each Morse/distinct function, so sigma counts each finite H0 bar of F exactly once as an ordered maximum/merger pair, with lifetimes A ell^H_i. (c) Pair formula ST (3)/SG (11): for fixed s and any nonnegative Borel mark w(p,q,.), w(p,q,s .) is again a nonnegative Borel mark of the C4 field, so SG (11) applied to H with mark w(p,q,sH) and the identities p^(sH)_(grad)(0) = s^(-2d) p^H_(grad)(0), E^(sH)[Delta^(sH) w(sH) | grads = 0] = s^(2d) E^H[Delta^H w(sH) | grads = 0] give (11) for sH with the dilated versions; integrating P_A(ds) on both sides (Tonelli, both sides in [0,infinity]) gives (3) for F with the unnormalized mixture version kappa of P3. (d) Two-height kernel: (T2) defines the F-version K^F_sel of ST (4)/SG (12), Borel in (p,q,b,b') by Tonelli, and (T3) is the resulting density identity (ST line 104: Tonelli as a density identity). Finiteness at every fiber with p != q and ell = b - b' > 0: for the fixed pair (p,q), the O_(p,q) covariance is positive definite (SG (9), two-site value/gradient rank at every distinct pair), so, as in P4(b) but with pair-specific constants, K^H_sel(p,q,b',s') <= K^H_cand(p,q,b',s') <= C_(p,q) (1+|b'|+|s'|)^(2d) exp(-c_(p,q)(b'^2+s'^2)); at (b',s') = (b/A,(b-ell)/A), b'^2+s'^2 >= ell^2/(2A^2), so A^(-2) K^H_sel(p,q,b/A,(b-ell)/A) <= C_(p,q) A^(-2) (1+(|b|+|b-ell|)/A)^(2d) exp(-c_(p,q) ell^2/(2A^2)) <= M_(p,q)(b,ell) < infinity by P5 (N = 2), uniformly in A. Hence K^F_sel(p,q,b,b-ell) <= M_(p,q)(b,ell) < infinity for every law of A. (At ell = 0 fibers, and for the gradient-only product at grad = 0, the mixture can be +infinity when E[A^(-2d)] = infinity; see gap G2. These fibers are never consumed: lifetimes are positive and ST evaluates COUNT through (4).) Also nu_F(ell) < infinity at every ell > 0 for every law of A: by P4(c), on {A >= ell}, A^(-1) nu_H(ell/A) <= G ell^(-1/3) A^(-2/3) <= G ell^(-1); on {A < ell}, ell/A > 1 and A^(-1) nu_H(ell/A) <= C A^(-1) exp(-c ell^2/A^2) <= C'/ell. So (T3) is a finite nonnegative Borel density with total mass E B_H/V.

CONTACT. Fix (u,b,k), k > 0 (x plays no role on the stationary torus, SG line 344-345). Density part: pi^F_r(v_r(b,k)) = E[A^(-(2d+2)) pi^H_r(v_r(b/A,k/A))] by P3. For 0 < r <= r_0 SG gives Sigma^H_r >= (lambda/2) I and Sigma^H_r <= Lambda I (lines 345-347) and |v_r(b',k')|^2 >= c(b'^2+k'^2) (lines 385-387), so pi^H_r(v_r(b',k')) <= C exp(-c(b'^2+k'^2)/(2 Lambda)) uniformly in r <= r_0. The dominating function of A is C A^(-(2d+2)) exp(-c(b^2+k^2)/(2 Lambda A^2)), bounded on (0,infinity) by P5 (N = 2d+2, no polynomial factor), hence P_A-integrable for every law. Pointwise, pi^H_r(v_r(b/A,k/A)) -> pi^H_0(v_0(b/A,k/A)) as r -> 0 (SG lines 347-348, CONTACT density part at the mark (b/A,k/A)). Dominated convergence: pi^F_r(v_r) -> pi^F_0(v_0) := E[A^(-(2d+2)) pi^H_0(v_0/A)], which by P3 at r = 0 is the density of U_0 F at v_0; it is finite (same bound) and strictly positive (pi^H_0 > 0 everywhere since Sigma_0 is positive definite). Weight part: by (T1), P^F_r(b,k) = E[A^(-2) P^H_r(b/A,k/A)], with 0 <= P^H_r <= H_SG for r <= r_0 (SG (19), which is precisely the all-mark bound on 12 pi_r(v_r) E_(Q_r) V_r). Dominating function A^(-2) H_SG(b/A,k/A) = C A^(-2) (1+(|b|+k)/A)^(2d) exp(-c(b^2+k^2)/A^2) <= M_2(b,k) by P5, integrable for every law. Pointwise, P^H_r(b',k') -> P^H_0(b',k') := 12 pi^H_0(v_0) z^H_0 (SG lines 380-385: E_(Q_r) V_r -> z_0, density convergence), with P^H_0 > 0 everywhere (z_0 > 0 at every b in R, k > 0, SG lines 383-385). Dominated convergence: P^F_r -> P^F_0 := E[A^(-2) P^H_0(b/A,k/A)] in (0,infinity). Therefore E_(Q^F_r)[V_r] = P^F_r/(12 pi^F_r(v_r)) -> P^F_0/(12 pi^F_0(v_0)) =: z^F_0, finite and positive; by (P3a) at r = 0, z^F_0 = E_(Q^F_0)[V_0] = 36 k^2 E_(Q^F_0)[(det A_0)^2 1{A_0 < 0}], the literal form in ST's CONTACT row (ST line 45) for the mixture conditional law Q^F_0. Both quantities are finite, as ST requires.

SELECT. By (T1) with sigma scale-invariant (P1), Phi^F_r(b,k) = 12 pi^F_r(v_r) E_(Q^F_r)[V_r(1-sigma)] = E[A^(-2) Phi^H_r(b/A,k/A)]; 0 <= Phi^H_r <= P^H_r <= H_SG, so the same dominating function applies; pointwise Phi^H_r(b',k') -> 0 by SG (21) (lines 462-465). Dominated convergence gives Phi^F_r -> 0, and dividing by pi^F_r(v_r) -> pi^F_0(v_0) > 0 gives E_(Q^F_r)[V_r(1-sigma)] -> 0, i.e. SELECT (ST line 46) at every fixed fiber. In particular B^F_r = P^F_r - Phi^F_r -> P^F_0 = 12 pi^F_0(v_0) z^F_0, the F-analogue of ST line 388.

Where boundedness or moments of A would enter: nowhere in (i). Every dominating function is a bounded function of A (P5), because the Gaussian factor exp(-c k^2/A^2) with k > 0 controls A -> 0 and the explicit negative powers control A -> infinity.
proofs.hypotheses_used: P1-P5; SG Section 4 (236-311) COUNT for H; SG (9) two-site rank; SG lines 343-348 covariance floor/upper bound and density convergence; SG (19); SG lines 380-385 (V_r -> V_0, z_0 > 0 finite); SG (21); ST contracts table lines 44-46; ST (3)-(5) (88-102, 125-139); ST line 383-388. No hypothesis on A beyond A > 0 a.s. and independence.

proofs.part: (ii) ENVELOPE holds for F iff m < infinity; the explicit envelope and its k^(-2/3)-mass
proofs.proof:
Define H^F(b,k) := E[A^(-2) H_SG(b/A,k/A)] in [0,infinity]. It is finite at every (b,k), k > 0, for every law of A (P5 with N = 2), Borel by Tonelli, and nonnegative; it does not depend on u (SG's H_SG does not), and on the flat torus not on x.

If m < infinity, ENVELOPE holds. Domination: for 0 < r <= r_0 (SG's r_0, line 346), (T1) and SG (19) applied at the mark (b/A,k/A) in R x (0,infinity) (where (19) holds for every mark and every r <= r_0; r is the physical separation, unchanged by amplitude) give P^F_r(b,k) = E[A^(-2) P^H_r(b/A,k/A)] <= E[A^(-2) H_SG(b/A,k/A)] = H^F(b,k), hence 12 pi^F_r(v_r) E_(Q^F_r)[V_r] <= H^F for 0 < r <= r_0 as in ST line 47. Integrability: by Tonelli (nonnegative integrand), integral_R integral_0^infinity k^(-2/3) H^F db dk = E[ A^(-2) integral_R integral_0^infinity k^(-2/3) H_SG(b/A,k/A) db dk ]. For each fixed a > 0 the linear change of variables b = a b', k = a k' maps R x (0,infinity) onto itself with Jacobian a^2 and k^(-2/3) = a^(-2/3) k'^(-2/3); so the inner integral equals a^(-2) a^2 a^(-2/3) I_SG = a^(-2/3) I_SG with I_SG = integral k^(-2/3) H_SG < infinity (SG (19) line 394). Therefore
   integral k^(-2/3) H^F db dk = E[A^(-2/3)] I_SG = m I_SG,
and with the direction integral, |S^(d-1)| m I_SG, finite iff m < infinity. Hence H^F is an envelope for F with SG's r_0 when m < infinity. Note that the substitution is performed at fixed a before any expectation and needs no integrability of A anywhere: E[A^(-2/3); A >= 1] <= 1 for every law, so m < infinity is a condition on the law of A near 0 only; unboundedness of A is irrelevant. (Tails: if A is unbounded, H^F has non-Gaussian mark tails, e.g. H^F(b,k) >= C e^(-c) E[A^(-2); A >= |b|+k]; the integrability is nonetheless exact by the identity above, no tail estimate is needed.)

If m = infinity, no envelope exists. Suppose r_0' > 0 and a nonnegative Borel H'(u,b,k) satisfy 12 pi^F_r(v_r) E_(Q^F_r)[V_r] <= H'(u,b,k) for all 0 < r <= r_0' (for the specified mixture versions; an a.e.-in-(b,k) inequality for each r suffices) and integral k^(-2/3) H' db dk d sigma < infinity. By (i), P^F_r(b,k) -> P^F_0(b,k) = E[A^(-2) P^H_0(b/A,k/A)] pointwise as r -> 0 (take r = r_n -> 0 along a sequence if the bound is only a.e.), so P^F_0 <= H' (a.e.). Hence integral k^(-2/3) H' >= integral k^(-2/3) P^F_0 db dk d sigma = E[ A^(-2) integral k^(-2/3) P^H_0(b/A,k/A) db dk d sigma ] (Tonelli) = E[A^(-2/3)] integral k^(-2/3) P^H_0 db dk d sigma (same substitution at fixed a) = m * 12 * (c_q/4) = 3 m c_q, using SG (24) (lines 504-507): c_q = 4 integral k^(-2/3) pi_0(v_0) z_0 db dk d sigma and P^H_0 = 12 pi_0(v_0) z_0. Since c_q > 0 (SG line 509 'finite and positive'; SG line 545 D_u > 0) and m = infinity, the right side is +infinity, contradicting integral k^(-2/3) H' < infinity. Thus ENVELOPE fails for every candidate (r_0', H'), direction-dependent or not. The obstruction is the contact limit itself: the k^(-2/3)-mass of the F-contact amplitude is 3 m c_q, so any envelope must carry infinite mass. This is the precise sense in which ST's 'small-amplitude tails' falsifier (ST line 47) is realized.
proofs.hypotheses_used: (T1); SG (19) at every mark and 0 < r <= r_0 (lines 388-394); SG (24) and c_q > 0 (lines 504-509); (i) for the pointwise contact limit; Tonelli; the exact linear change of variables at fixed amplitude. ST line 47 (ENVELOPE row). No bound or moment on A other than m itself.

proofs.part: (iii) m < infinity: FAR for F, the density and count asymptotics by dominated convergence, and consistency with ST's theorem
proofs.proof:
Assume m < infinity. Write g(u) = u^(1/3) nu_H(u), g_far(u) = u^(1/3) nu_(H,far)(u), h(u) = u^(-2/3) m_H(u), with the bounds of P4: 0 <= g <= G, 0 <= g_far <= G_far, 0 <= h <= (3/2) G, g(u) -> C_H, g_far(u) -> 0, h(u) -> (3/2) C_H as u -> 0.

FAR. By (T3) restricted to dist(p,q) >= r_0 (same r_0 as in (ii)), nu^F_far(ell) = E[A^(-1) nu_(H,far)(ell/A)], so ell^(1/3) nu^F_far(ell) = E[A^(-2/3) g_far(ell/A)]. Dominating function: G_far A^(-2/3), integrable because m < infinity (and G_far < infinity by P4(b), see gap G1). Pointwise: for each fixed A > 0, ell/A -> 0, and g_far(ell/A) <= C (ell/A)^(1/3) -> 0 by SG (22). Dominated convergence along any sequence ell_n -> 0: ell^(1/3) nu^F_far(ell) -> 0. Finiteness and local integrability: nu^F_far(ell) <= G_far m ell^(-1/3) < infinity for every ell > 0, locally integrable on (0,infinity); Borel by Tonelli. This is FAR in exactly ST's form (ST line 48: 'finite, locally integrable Borel lifetime density nu_far with ell^(1/3) nu_far -> 0'). The uniform O(1) far candidate bound that SG has for H (SG (22)) is NOT claimed for F: ST line 48 lists it only as sufficient, and AMP (17) (lines 290-299) shows it can fail for F even when m < infinity (power law with 2/3 < alpha < 1).

Density asymptotic, directly from the transform. By (T3), ell^(1/3) nu_F(ell) = E[ A^(-2/3) (ell/A)^(1/3) nu_H(ell/A) ] = E[A^(-2/3) g(ell/A)]. Dominating function: G A^(-2/3) with G = sup_(u>0) g(u) < infinity (P4(c)); it is P_A-integrable iff m < infinity. This is the only place where the GLOBAL sup (including large lifetimes u) is needed: small amplitudes A send the argument ell/A to arbitrarily large lifetimes, and a bound of g only on (0,1] would leave E[A^(-1) nu_H(ell/A); A < ell] uncontrolled (for laws with E[A^(-2/3)] < infinity = E[A^(-1); A < ell] this term cannot be handled without decay of nu_H at infinity). Pointwise: for every fixed A > 0, g(ell/A) -> C_H as ell -> 0 by SG (4), which is a pointwise statement for the canonical representative (SG lines 508-512) - essential, since the transform evaluates nu_H at the points ell/A. Dominated convergence along any sequence ell_n -> 0 gives lim ell^(1/3) nu_F(ell) = E[A^(-2/3)] C_H = m C_H, i.e. nu_F(ell) ~ m C_H ell^(-1/3).

Count asymptotic. By (T4), t^(-2/3) m_F(t) = E[A^(-2/3) h(t/A)]. Dominating function (3/2) G A^(-2/3) (or, using only the small-u asymptotic and finite total mass, max(C, delta^(-2/3) E B_H/V) A^(-2/3) by P4(d)), integrable since m < infinity; pointwise h(t/A) -> (3/2) C_H (SG (4), count form). Dominated convergence: E N^F_t / V = m_F(t) ~ (3/2) m C_H t^(2/3). (Equivalently, integrate the density asymptotic: integral_0^t ell^(-1/3) d ell = (3/2) t^(2/3), ST line 432.) The count statement thus needs only SG (4) and finite total mass, not the global density bound.

Consistency with ST. By (i), (ii) and FAR above, F satisfies COUNT, CONTACT, SELECT, ENVELOPE (r_0, H^F) and FAR with the specified mixture versions, and ST's theorem (lines 59-65) applies to F provided its coefficient is positive. ST (14) (lines 424-427) for F, with the stationary torus cancelling V_X (ST lines 445-447, SG 492-493): C_F = 4 integral k^(-2/3) pi^F_0(v_0) z^F_0 db dk d sigma = (4/12) integral k^(-2/3) P^F_0 db dk d sigma = (1/3) * 3 m c_q = m c_q = m C_H, using the computation in (ii) (integral k^(-2/3) P^F_0 = 3 m c_q) - which is the substitution b = A b', k = A k' at fixed A followed by Tonelli; nothing about A at infinity is needed. C_F > 0 since m > 0 and c_q > 0. ST's representative is the near/far split of the kernel (4) for F, i.e. of K^F_sel in (T2); its (b,p,q)-integral is literally (T3), so ST's theorem and the direct transform concern the same canonical Borel representative and give the same pointwise limit m C_H. ST's near-part dominated convergence (lines 415-427) for F uses the bounded-J version of k^(-2/3) H^F (J = 1 on the flat torus) and the pointwise limits of (i); its far part is FAR above. Hence the two derivations agree, as claimed.

proofs.part: (iv) m = infinity: divergence of ell^(1/3) nu_F(ell) by Fatou
proofs.proof: Assume m = infinity. By (T3) (a Tonelli identity in [0,infinity], valid for every law of A), ell^(1/3) nu_F(ell) = E[A^(-2/3) g(ell/A)] with g(u) = u^(1/3) nu_H(u) >= 0 for the canonical representative, which is a nonnegative Borel function (SG (12), line 303-306; nonnegativity is what Fatou needs). Let ell_n -> 0 be any sequence and f_n := A^(-2/3) g(ell_n/A) >= 0, measurable. Fatou's lemma: liminf_n E[f_n] >= E[liminf_n f_n]. For every fixed A > 0, ell_n/A -> 0, and g(ell_n/A) -> C_H by SG (4) (pointwise for the canonical representative, lines 508-512), so liminf_n f_n = lim_n f_n = A^(-2/3) C_H. Hence liminf_n ell_n^(1/3) nu_F(ell_n) >= C_H E[A^(-2/3)] = C_H m = +infinity, because C_H = c_q > 0 (SG line 509). Since this holds for every sequence ell_n -> 0, lim_(ell -> 0) ell^(1/3) nu_F(ell) = +infinity. On 'liminf being the right notion': Fatou puts liminf inside the expectation; here the inside limit exists (SG (4) is a limit, not merely liminf_u u^(1/3) nu_H(u) = C_H), so the lower bound is E[A^(-2/3) C_H]; had only liminf_u g(u) = C_H been available, the same argument would still give liminf_ell ell^(1/3) nu_F(ell) >= C_H m = infinity, so the conclusion is insensitive to that distinction. No upper bound on g, no large-lifetime control, no moment on A and no boundedness is used. The same Fatou argument with (T4) and h(u) -> (3/2) C_H gives t^(-2/3) m_F(t) -> infinity. Consequently no finite C satisfies nu_F(ell) ~ C ell^(-1/3): the -1/3 law fails, and it fails by an excess of short bars (ratio -> infinity), in agreement with ST's lower-bound falsifier (24) (lines 672-674) and AMP (12), (14). Remark: nu_F(ell) itself is finite at every ell > 0 for every law of A (shown in (i)), so the divergence is of the ratio ell^(1/3) nu_F(ell), not of the density values; and when m = infinity, ENVELOPE fails by (ii) while FAR may or may not hold (not needed and not claimed).

Fatou's lemma. No other hypothesis; in particular no large-lifetime bound (P4(b)) and no property of A besides A > 0 and independence.

proofs.part: Consequences: the exact amplitude class, AMP (16), and scope
proofs.proof:
Class. By (iii), m < infinity implies nu_F ~ m C_H ell^(-1/3); by (iv), m = infinity implies ell^(1/3) nu_F -> infinity. Hence among independent positive multiplicative amplitudes of an SG-admitted H, the -1/3 law holds exactly for {A : E[A^(-2/3)] < infinity}, always with coefficient E[A^(-2/3)] C_H, and the count law E N^F_t/V ~ (3/2) E[A^(-2/3)] C_H t^(2/3) holds on the same class (its failure on the complement is also by (iv)). The dichotomy is governed by the law of A near 0 only: E[A^(-2/3); A >= 1] <= 1 for every law. The coefficient identity m C_H is the mixture of ST's unit check C_(aH) = a^(-2/3) C_H (ST lines 507-513), and it is exactly ST's amplitude-scaling diagnostic at lines 676-679 ('E R^(-2/3) is infinite, matching C_(aH) = a^(-2/3) C_H') turned into a theorem.

AMP (16). AMP's amplitude (6) (line 120) is A = aR with density alpha a^(-alpha) u^(alpha-1) on (0,a), a = sqrt((alpha+2)/alpha). Then E[A^(-2/3)] = alpha a^(-alpha) integral_0^a u^(alpha-5/3) du = alpha a^(-alpha) a^(alpha-2/3)/(alpha-2/3) = a^(-2/3) alpha/(alpha-2/3) for alpha > 2/3, and = +infinity for alpha <= 2/3. This is AMP's E A^(-beta) = a^(-beta) alpha/(alpha-beta) in (16) (line 257), so (iii) reproduces AMP (16) (density and count), and (iv) reproduces the failure of the -1/3 law in AMP's regimes alpha < 2/3 (12) and alpha = 2/3 (14) - as a divergence statement only; the finer rates t^(alpha-1) and t^(beta-1) log(1/t) are specific to the power law and are not part of the general theorem. AMP Section 5 lines 305-310 declined to state a general small-amplitude law ('Different amplitude tails require their own integral analysis'); the present theorem is that statement for independent multiplicative amplitudes: the integral analysis reduces to the single number E[A^(-2/3)].

Scope. Not covered: (a) the iid-copy process (Poisson) limits, which require the mixed cluster estimate E[N_F(Tt) 1{N_F(Tt) >= 2}] = o(t^(2/3)) from AMP (2)/SG (28) and are stated only for the power law in AMP Section 10 (the same dominated-convergence pattern with AMP (20) as majorant is plausible for m < infinity but is not proved here); (b) amplitudes not independent of H; (c) non-multiplicative non-Gaussian fields, for which none of the scaling identities P1-P3 hold. The theorem says nothing about whether F satisfies any contract with better-than-required bounds (e.g. a uniform far bound).

gaps_or_corrections: G1 (re-derivation needed, not in SG verbatim): the density statement of (iii) uses sup_{u>0} u^(1/3) nu_H(u) < infinity over ALL lifetimes, including u -> infinity, because small amplitudes map ell/A to large lifetimes. SG supplies this for the near part (its representation at lines 498-502 with (19) gives g_near <= K_near for every u) but for the far part SG displays (22) only on 0 < ell <= 1 plus 'a finite local bound on any fixed compact positive-lifetime band' (lines 481-482). The global bound nu_(H,far)(ell) <= C_far (1+ell)^(2d) exp(-ell^2/(4 Lambda)) for all ell > 0 is obtained by repeating SG's own argument (lines 473-480: separated-pair covariance floor and upper bound, Gaussian regression, 2d-th C2 moment) while keeping ell inside the Gaussian exponent (b^2 + (b-ell)^2 >= ell^2/2); this is done in P4(b). It uses nothing beyond SG's hypotheses, but it is a step not literally present in SG. The count statement of (iii) and all of (i), (ii), (iv) do not need it.

G2 (qualification to the literal wording of COUNT): the F-side gradient-only density p^F_(grad F(p),grad F(q))(0) = E[A^(-2d)] p^H(0) is +infinity when E[A^(-2d)] = infinity (e.g. AMP's power law with alpha <= 2d), so at the zero-gradient fiber the factorization 'density times conditional expectation' in ST (3)/SG (11) degenerates (infinity times 0) and must be read in the unnormalized-mixture form kappa of P3, which is finite whenever the H-side product is. Likewise the two-height mixture kernel can be +infinity on the diagonal ell = 0 fibers (and at ell > 0 it is finite at every fiber for every law of A, P5). This is why the claim's qualifier 'finite mixture versions at every fiber with ell > 0' is necessary and cannot be dropped. The structural theorem consumes COUNT only through (4) at ell > 0, so nothing downstream is affected.

G3 (scope of FAR for F): FAR holds in ST's required sense (finite, locally integrable, ell^(1/3) nu_far -> 0), but the uniform O(1) far candidate bound SG (22) does not in general transfer to F (AMP (17), lines 290-299, shows nu_(F,far) unbounded for 2/3 < alpha < 1). The claim's wording 'FAR holds' is correct; a reader must not infer the O(1) bound.

G4 (versions): all F-side statements are for the A-mixture versions of densities and conditional laws (P3), which are the versions COUNT for F supplies and which ST lines 115-120 fix as the representative; the 'no envelope when m = infinity' statement is robust to changing these versions on Lebesgue-null (b,k) sets (the obstruction is an integral), but it is a statement about the specified versions, not about every conceivable version.

G5 (wording in the claim for (iv)): the claim says 'liminf_u u^(1/3) nu_H(u) = C_H > 0'; SG (4) actually gives the limit, so liminf = lim. The Fatou step is correct either way; with the limit the conclusion is lim ell^(1/3) nu_F = infinity along every sequence.

G6 (tails of the envelope, a remark not a gap): for unbounded A the envelope H^F has non-Gaussian mark tails (H^F(b,k) >= C e^(-c) E[A^(-2); A >= |b|+k]); its k^(-2/3)-integrability is nevertheless exact (= m I_SG) because the substitution b = A b', k = A k' is performed at fixed A with Jacobian A^2 and no integrability of A at infinity is used. Boundedness of A is never used in (i)-(iv); it enters only AMP's specific formulas (cutoff t/a in AMP (10), Mellin-moment bookkeeping).

G7 (numerical caveat): the first direct 3-d quadrature of the envelope identity, with a law charging A -> 0 (AMP alpha = 1, uniform on (0, sqrt 3)) and a fixed b-grid of spacing 0.67, returned a ratio of 324 to m I_SG; this was a resolution artifact (the Gaussian H_SG(b/a,k/a) has width a in b and is unresolved for a << 0.67), not a failure of the identity; with resolved grids and laws supported on [0.02, 50] the ratios are 0.995, 1.011, 0.9997. The identity is exact by the change of variables; the numerics only check the implementation.

No correction to the mathematical content of the claim is needed: (i)-(iv) and the consequence are proved as stated, with G1 supplying one re-derived input and G2 refining the fiber statement of COUNT.
